newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN 13-WK T-BILL AVG YIELD HITS 19.9 PCT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN 13-WK T-BILL AVG YIELD HITS 19.9 PCT.

text.p: Average yield at the Finance Ministry's auction of 13-week treasury bills on Wednesday rose to 19.926 percent from 18.248 percent in the last auction of similar T-bills on July 16, the central bank (NBS) said.
The ministry accepted bids worth 1.615 billion crowns ($46.6 million) out of total demand of 1.915 billion crowns, the NBS said in a statement.
The minimum accepted yield was 18.00 percent, while the maximum yield hit 22.50 percent.
The ministry does not announce an amount on offer at state securities auctions or set a minimum or maximum limit price on bids.
In the finance ministry's last auction of state securities on August 6, a 1.257-billion crown tranche of four-week T-bills was sold at an average yield of 19.287 percent.

The finance ministry uses T-bills and state bonds as the main tools to cover the state budget deficit, which widened to 17.936 billion crowns in the first seven months from 13.209 billion in the first half.
The ministry also issued a special 4.016 billion crown tranche of one-week T-bills on Wednesday to the NBS's portfolio at an undisclosed rate.
The central bank regularly takes state securities into its portfolio to help the finance ministry refinance a growing state budget deficit.
But under current legislation, the NBS can only hold state paper totalling five percent of budget revenues in the previous fiscal year. Budget revenues totalled 166.3 billion crowns in 1996.
